title: Wet mopping with a bucket and wringer
audience: Cleaners who wet mop hard floors with a conventional bucket and wringer, in offices, shared buildings and homes.
learningOutcomes: Prepare the floor and the solution so the wet mopping starts with a clean, dry-soil-free surface.
Wring and load the mop so that the floor is damp, not flooded.
Tackle corners and edges before the open floor, working toward the exit so that no finished floor is walked on.

instruction.heading: Clear the floor before the water goes down
instruction.body: Wet mopping only works on a floor that has already been dust mopped or vacuumed. Before the bucket comes in, lift any mats and scrape off adhesive labels and chewing gum with a putty knife, held at a shallow angle so the floor is not gouged. Set out wet floor signs by each room entrance so people know the floor is wet and do not walk onto it while it dries.

instruction.heading: Make up the solution and wring the mop
instruction.body: Fill the bucket with cold water to the marked level, then add pH-neutral floor detergent at the dose on the product label. Do not add more than the label allows, because excess product leaves a film. Dunk the head, then run it through the wringer and press the handle down to squeeze out the surplus. The head should be damp, not dripping. A head that is too wet floods the floor, and one that is too dry lifts less soil.

instruction.heading: The mopping stroke and order
instruction.body: Stand upright and keep your back neutral. Avoid twisting at the waist. Mop the corners and edges before the open floor, using the head to reach into the angles. Fill the open floor by moving the mop in a looping pattern that carries you backward toward the exit. Keep the bucket on the unwashed side and behind your body, so that you never step onto a section you have just mopped. Overlap each stroke by a short distance so that no strip is missed. Re-wring the mop whenever the head is no longer damp, and replace the bucket water once it looks soiled, because dirty water puts soil back on the floor.

instruction.heading: Finish, dry and tidy up
instruction.body: When the last area is done, take the bucket and wringer back to the cleaning cupboard rather than leaving them in the room. Remove the wet floor signs only when the floor has dried. A floor that still shows a sheen or a streak has not been cleaned properly, so check the finish before you move on. If the floor shows a film, a scrub or a recoat may be needed, and that should be reported to the supervisor rather than attempted with the wet mop alone.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection before handling chemicals.
Lift mats and scrape adhesive labels and chewing gum off with a putty knife.
Set out wet floor signs by the room entrances.
Fill the bucket with cold water to the marked level, and add pH-neutral floor detergent at the label dose.
Squeeze the head through the wringer until it is damp, not dripping.
Stand upright and mop the corners and edges, then the open floor in overlapping looping passes toward the exit.
Re-wring the head as needed and change the bucket water when it looks soiled.
Return the bucket and wringer to the cleaning cupboard, drain and flush them, and store them.
Remove the wet floor signs once the floor has fully dried, then check the finish.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner in an office corridor mops with the bucket water after the water has turned grey, and the floor now looks streaky with a faint film.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What caused the streaks, and what should the cleaner do?
workedExamples.reasoning: Dirty water spreads soil back onto the floor and leaves a film. The bucket water should have been replaced once it looked soiled. Mop again with clean solution, and report the film to the supervisor if it does not clear.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner starts a wet mop in the middle of a large room, then walks back across the floor to reach the door.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the correct approach for this room?
workedExamples.reasoning: Start at the far corners and work toward the exit so that the cleaner moves backward over clean floor, not over wet floor. Keep the bucket behind you on the unmopped part.

equipmentAndPpe: Wet mop head fitted with a clean, undamaged mop head or microfiber head.
pH-neutral floor detergent, dosed to the label.
Putty knife and a broom or dust mop.
Cloth for drying the bucket and wringer.

commonErrors.error: Using a mop head that is dripping, which floods the floor and leaves a slippery surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Wring the head until it is damp, and re-wring it during the job.
Change the water once it looks soiled, and use the marked fill level.

commonErrors.error: Twisting at the waist while mopping.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the spine straight and move the mop with the arms and the hips square to the work.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the wet floor sign in place after the floor has dried, or removing it while the floor is still wet.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the sign only when the floor has dried, and check the surface before the room is reopened.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Keep the work area marked with signs while the floor is wet, so people do not slip.
Stand upright and use the legs to reach. Do not twist the spine to reach into corners, and ask for help with heavy buckets.
Wear gloves and eye protection when mixing and handling floor detergent, and keep gloves on whenever you handle a mop head.

qualityStandard: All floor areas are mopped, including corners and edges.
No debris, adhesive labels or chewing gum remain on the floor.
The floor has no streaks, film or black heel marks once dry.
The wet floor signs are in place while the floor is wet and removed once dry.
The bucket and wringer are emptied, rinsed and stored.
documentationEvidence: Job record of the area mopped, with the date, time and product used.
Note of any floor that has a film or stain that did not clear, for supervisor review.
summary: Dust mop or vacuum first, then remove labels and gum, then mop.
Dose the solution to the label and use the marked fill level.
Wring the head until damp, and change the water when it looks soiled.
Tackle corners and edges before the open floor, moving toward the exit, and check the finish once dry.

knowledgeChecks.question: How wet should a bucket mop head be before it is used on a floor?
options: Dripping, so that the floor is fully soaked
Damp, so that it lifts soil without flooding the floor
Dry, so that the water is applied only by the floor cleaner

knowledgeChecks.question: In what order should a room be mopped?
options: The exit first, then the corners as the cleaner walks out
The centre first, then the corners, then the exit
Corners and edges, then the open floor moving toward the exit

knowledgeChecks.question: When should the bucket water be changed?
options: Once it looks soiled, so that dirty water is not spread across the floor
Only at the far end of the week, to save product
After the last room, once the floor cleaner has been added at the start
